summary: Full backend + frontend testing of the new JWT auth feature (email/password login for buyers & admin, wishlist, /me/orders, guest checkout). 18/18 pytest tests PASS covering register (happy path, short password rejection, duplicate email), login (wrong/right password), /api/auth/me, wishlist toggle+GET+auth-required, guest Midtrans checkout, authed Midtrans checkout writing user_id, /me/orders returns order with delivery_info hidden while pending, /payments/status hides delivery_info until paid, admin JWT login (admin@willjustplay.com/Musangpandan123), /api/admin/verify accepting admin JWT and rejecting buyer JWT, legacy x-admin-key still accepted, admin CRUD on /admin/products via JWT. Frontend Playwright: Masuk button opens auth-modal; register auto-logs in and shows nav-account-link + nav-logout-button; logout clears session; wrong password shows inline 'Email atau password salah' via [data-testid=auth-error]; duplicate email shows 'Email sudah terdaftar'; wishlist heart toggles and persists across reload (heart element shows coral/fill class); /akun page renders account-tab-orders + account-tab-wishlist + account-wishlist-grid; /admin with buyer JWT shows 'bukan admin' [data-testid=admin-not-authorized]; /admin login with admin creds loads dashboard tabs (products/orders/testimonials), product rows load, testimonials tab loads. Do not have real order under Pesanan tab because live Midtrans not triggered from UI (per instructions), but backend test confirms authed checkout creates order tied to user_id with hidden delivery_info.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py get_optional_user swallows all invalid tokens as None — good; but token expiry produces same behavior as guest. Consider returning 401 on invalid-but-present token for /me/* routes (currently get_current_user handles this correctly via user_from_request returning None).

Admin seed on startup updates password if changed (good idempotency). CORS allow_credentials=True with allow_origins='*' is technically invalid per spec but harmless because frontend uses Bearer header, not cookies.
require_admin still accepts legacy x-admin-key header — intended per spec. Fine.
bcrypt hash uses standard $2b$ prefix (verified via register-then-login round trip).
